contexts.text: a. (The doctrines of the Lutherans concerning the Person of Christ, and concerning the Holy Supper.) AR 13. a.

(Lutherans seen who could not say Divine Human, although) the Augsburg Confession, and Luther himself, have taught that the Son of God and the Sou of Man in Christ are one Person; and that He Himself also as to His human nature is the True, Omnipotent, and Eternal God... TCR 111:10.
They confessed that they had been Lutherans.
(The nature of the faith of the Lutherans shown by its sphere.)
Such things as relate to vastation are mainly concerning the Lutherans, and the Reformed so called.
Christians hold the middle who are called Lutherans, and the Reformed...
On those who make the Lutheran religion to be of the life.
(The Lutheran Church does not teach faith alone when it teaches from the Word.) AE 885:5, Shown.
